title: There Is No Planet B: Aligning Stakeholder Interests to Preserve the Amazon Rainforest
eligible_reason: Natura's entry into Amazon municipalities is a binary treatment switching on at municipality-specific years (13 in-sample first-treatment years, 2000-2018; 704 never-treated municipalities). Table 2 columns without controls and the Table 4/5 mechanism regressions are static TWFE with municipality and year FE and no controls.
design_notes: Balanced municipality-year panel, 760 Legal Amazon municipalities x 19 years (2000-2018). Treatment Natura = 1[year >= Natura_start]. First-treatment years (municipalities): 2000 (4, always treated: Natura_start 1999 or 2000), 2001 (3), 2002 (1), 2003 (2), 2004 (2), 2006 (10), 2008 (5), 2009 (5), 2011 (7), 2014 (5), 2015 (6), 2017 (5), 2018 (1). Outcomes: ln_forested, ln_fire (INPE), and 8 IBGE agricultural census outcomes. SEs clustered by municipality. The paper's headline identification is the IV in Table 3 (missing satellite images instrument), which is ineligible; the TWFE DiD in Table 2 is reported first in the main text. Figure 3 is an eventdd event study with controls.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 13 in-sample first-treatment years; 12 have untreated pre-period observations (the 2000 cohort of 4 municipalities is always treated).

screener_notes: Screened from the package only. Full-text flags show the paper cites Callaway-Sant'Anna, Goodman-Bacon and de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille, but no modern estimator appears in the code. Only 56 treated municipalities (7.4%) with small cohorts (1-10 municipalities), so cohort-level ATTs will be noisy. Single do-file; data from INPE, IBGE and Natura included in the package.
